question: Should OpenClaw add an operator-owned `agents.defaults` / per-agent prompt-rules config surface, and what write boundary should protect it?
rationale: Source review proves the feature is still missing, but adding a model-facing config/default prompt surface changes safety, session behavior, and Codex-backed runtime precedence across multiple entry points.

options.title: Approve narrow operator-owned overlay
options.body: Add an append-only prompt/rules overlay resolved at session creation, inherited from defaults to per-agent config, and keep it out of agent-facing config mutation unless explicitly allowed.

options.title: Fold into broader prompt customization
options.body: Keep this issue open but settle the broader system-prompt customization design before adding any new config key.

options.title: Reject core config surface
options.body: Keep workspace files, channel prompts, plugins, and external tooling as the supported rule-management mechanisms and close this cluster as not planned.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow operator-owned overlay
recommendation.body: Add an append-only prompt/rules overlay resolved at session creation, inherited from defaults to per-agent config, and keep it out of agent-facing config mutation unless explicitly allowed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest prompt/config ownership trail and is the best available owner for a core prompt contract decision.
